reader.requirement: At --std 85, a WRITE (successful or not) to an indexed file must leave the file position indicator, a key value of the current key of reference (IX.4.5.4 GR4), unchanged, so the next sequential READ selects relative to the pre-WRITE indicator: the newly written record is returned when its key falls after the indicator (>= after OPEN/START, > or later-duplicate after READ), and a 'no valid next record' or at-end state survives the WRITE ('46').

edition-consulted.switches: whether the file-sharing facility (record locks, store attach) is in effect; consulted at OPEN/attach (IndexedConnector store attach, FileRegistry sharing posture), not by the FPI logic of WRITE or READ NEXT

reader.edition-search: grep -n Edition over src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/IO/*.cs; IndexedConnector#Write (lines 669-760) has no Edition/DialectBehavior reference and never writes _fpiKey, _readOrdinal, _positioner, FpiValid or LastReadUnsuccessful (grep of those fields shows writers only in OPEN, ReadSequential, ReadRandom and StartSucceeded). ReadSequential's edition switches (IndexedReadPreviousAfterOpenAtEnd for READ PREVIOUS, IndexedDuplicateKeyStatusSequentialOnly for the '02') do not select the record.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no (for the FPI; the sharing facility differs at 85 but does not reach this rule)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1c37_write_keeps_fpi is a RELATIVE-file case only and says so ('No indexed leg'); the indexed rule IX.4.9.4 GR5 is wholly unexercised by it: WRITE after OPEN, after READ, of a lower key, of a duplicate alternate key, a failed WRITE, and WRITE after at-end or failed START.

probes.printed: A0=00 A1=00 0000 (WRITE after OPEN I-O, then READ NEXT returns it); A2=00 AAAA; WRITE BBBB and 0001 (A3=00 A4=00), failed WRITE CCCC (W6 INV, A5=22); A6=00 BBBB A7=00 CCCC
probes.expected: GR4c after OPEN selects >= the lowest value; GR4d after READ AAAA selects the first key > AAAA, i.e. the newly written BBBB, never 0001; the failed WRITE changes nothing

probes.printed: B1=00 CCCC M300 (alternate key of reference with DUPLICATES); WRITE DDDD M300 and DDD1 M400; B2=00 DDDD M300 B3=00 DDD1 M400 B4=00 EEEE M500
probes.expected: GR4e: the duplicate released after the record just read is next, then the larger alternate values

probes.printed: B5=10, WRITE ZZZZ, B6=46; C1=23 (failed START), WRITE ZZZY C2=00, C3=46
probes.expected: the at-end and no-valid-next-record states survive the WRITE: '46' (IX.1.3.4 status 46 items 1 and 3)

reader.notes: The indexed FPI is a key value (_fpiKey) plus a duplicate ordinal and a validity bit, written only by OPEN, READ and START; WRITE never touches them, so READ NEXT after any WRITE selects from the pre-WRITE indicator. The witness was relative-only; the indexed probes, the rule's own subject, all matched the 1985 text.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:IX.1.3.3 (the FPI is affected only by CLOSE, OPEN, READ and START), IX.4.4.4 GR10 (OPEN sets the FPI to the lowest collating value), IX.4.5.4 GR4c-e (READ NEXT selects >= after OPEN/START, > after READ on a unique key, the next in arrival order within a duplicate set). Probe s2/w1.cob at --std 85, aimed at what the reader did not try (a WRITE whose key EQUALS the indicator, after the record that set it was deleted; a WRITE into the duplicate set the indicator stands in, after its record was deleted; ACCESS SEQUENTIAL OPEN I-O, where WRITE is not permitted (IX.4.4.4 GR4, Table 2)): dynamic: random READ BBBB P1=00, DELETE, WRITE FROM a new BBBB P2=00, READ NEXT P3=00 CCCCM300 (the new BBBB, key not greater than the indicator, skipped: GR4d); random READ KEY XA=M300 P4=02 CCCCM300, DELETE, WRITE FFFFM300 P5=02, READ NEXT P6=02 DDDDM300, P7=00 FFFFM300 (the order of the set kept: GR4e); sequential access I-O: READ Q1=00 AAAA, WRITE BBBB Q2=48 (USE ran), READ Q3=00 CCCC (the indicator survived the refused WRITE and nothing was written). Class c: WRITE ... WITH LOCK (2002) is refused at 85 (COBOL0900); OPEN EXTEND on a RANDOM file is refused (COBOL2372). cite.py: OK §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR5; OK §1985:IX.1.3.3; OK §1985:IX.4.5.4 GR4d; OK §1985:IX.4.5.4 GR4e; OK §1985:IX.4.4.4 GR4.
